diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive attenuation on this customer's fibre path. RX power declined from the normal range at approximately -19.2 dBm to the degraded range at -26.45 dBm over seven days, while TX power, TX bias current, and distance remained stable. The elevated session count and short sessions are consequences of the degrading optical link, not a separate authentication fault.
evidence: The customer's RX power fell from about -19.17 dBm, within the normal band, to -26.45 dBm, in the degraded band, so this is a genuine declining link.
TX power stayed near 2.3 dBm and TX bias current stayed around 11.1 mA, which rules against laser degradation.
Distance remained constant at 188 m, ruling out a path-record or fibre-route change.
The customer is currently online with a definite live ONU response, so this is not currently an onu_offline fault.
Peers on EPON0/3 have healthy optical levels, indicating the problem is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON port, splitter, or OLT.
The one offline peer is a single ONU among otherwise healthy peers and is consistent with normal background offline state, not a shared failure.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and OID queries, with healthy CPU, memory, temperature, and all tested PONs healthy.
The router heartbeat is healthy and VLAN 1013 is correctly provisioned, so neither router reachability nor VLAN 46 provisioning explains the issue.
There are 9 sessions in 24 hours with short average duration, but the optical decline takes precedence; the session flapping is a symptom of the degrading fibre.
PON traffic is not sufficient evidence of congestion, and the optical trend directly matches the customer's intermittent service complaint.

remediation.action: Dispatch field support to inspect and clean the customer's ONU and ODF/drop-fibre connectors, check for bends, damage, moisture, and bad splices, and perform an optical loss/OTDR test. Repair or replace the affected drop or splice as required. Continue monitoring RX power and session stability after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
